newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
A high-profile conference on the capital market has suggested formation of a special Economic Crime Detection Unit under the Home Ministry to stop stock market manipulation and bank frauds.
A national food and nutrition policy has targetted to increase the per head energy intake to 2279 kilo calorie by the year 2000 from current 1950 Kcal.

Opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia has accused Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's government of making the nation handicapped by announcing two-day weekly holiday as "part of evil designs by local and foreign powers."

Bangladesh capital Dhaka may have eight commuter railway lines and seven subway lines to ease the pressure on existing road network by year 2015, when the metropolitan city is expected to have a population of 17 million.
Hundreds of government employees on Sunday staged a rowdy demonstration inside Bangladesh Secretariat demanding rescinding of two-day weekly holiday and announcement of new pay-scale.

Dhaka's District & Session Judge Kazi Golam Rasul on Sunday referred the case records to the High Court for quashment of the proceedings against the businessmen accused of manipulating share prices during October to December last year.
Trade, industry and investment will be main areas of cooperation of the new economic block, comprising eight major OIC countries, to be launched in Istanbul in mid-June.
Law Minister Abdul Matin Khasru said on Sunday cumbersome judicial procedure would be removed by updating the laws to meet the demand of time.
